planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into humus-rich, well-drained woodland soil in shade to partial shade.

directions: Collected in Jackson County, Florida, this selection of native Allegheny spurge carries distinctively mottled, silver-spotted evergreen leaves that stand out against the plain green foliage of the typical species. Fragrant, bottlebrush-like white flower spikes emerge at the base of the plant in late winter before new leaves unfurl, often the earliest bloom in a shaded woodland bed. It spreads slowly into a dense, low mat rather than running aggressively, making it a well-behaved native alternative to Japanese pachysandra. Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade, and avoid wet, poorly drained sites where the crown can rot.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade.

directions: This Rohdea hybrid carries broad, glossy, upright evergreen leaves well taller than the typical dwarf Rohdea japonica cultivars, giving it a bolder architectural presence in a shaded bed. Like other Rohdea it is grown mainly for its handsome, long-lived evergreen foliage clump rather than its inconspicuous flowers, with a cluster of red berries following in fall on mature plants. Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade, where it tolerates dry shade and heavy root competition from trees far better than most shade perennials. It is extremely slow-growing and long-lived, needing only occasional division once a clump becomes overcrowded after many years.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade.

directions: This gold-spotted cast iron plant selection builds a dense clump of broad, glossy, dark green leaves heavily speckled with creamy gold, standing nearly two and a half feet tall at maturity. It tolerates deep, dry shade and heavy root competition better than almost any other broadleaf evergreen, making it reliable under established trees where little else will grow. Inconspicuous mottled flowers appear low at the soil surface in spring, easy to miss under the foliage canopy. Grow it in humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade, and divide only occasionally, since established clumps are slow to spread and resent frequent disturbance.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade.

directions: Giraffe carries glossy green leaves marked with creamy longitudinal streaks running the length of each blade, giving a patterned look reminiscent of its namesake animal's coat rather than the spotted pattern common in many Aspidistra selections. Reaching about two feet tall, it tolerates deep, dry shade and heavy root competition under established trees better than almost any other broadleaf evergreen. Inconspicuous flowers appear low at the soil surface in spring, easy to miss beneath the foliage. Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade, and divide only occasionally once a clump becomes congested after many years.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring into well-drained soil in full sun; Orange Blaze is a patented selection (PP31,545).

directions: Orange Blaze sends up sturdy, torch-like spikes of vivid orange tubular flowers over a compact clump of grassy, arching foliage, holding its color without fading through the heat of summer. Its moderate height keeps it in scale for a mid-border planting without the staking larger red hot pokers sometimes need. Hummingbirds visit the flower spikes heavily through the bloom season, and the foliage stays reasonably tidy between flushes. Grow in well-drained soil in full sun, and avoid winter-wet sites, since good drainage matters more to this plant's survival than cold alone.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring into average to moist, well-drained soil in full sun; discovered by plantsman Adam Black, this selection stays far more compact than the species.

directions: Black's Dwarf is a naturally compact selection of stiff bluestar that stays little more than a foot tall, a fraction of the four-plus feet the wild species can reach, while keeping the same narrow, willowy leaves and clusters of pale blue star-shaped spring flowers. Dark purple-black stems add a subtle color contrast beneath the foliage through the growing season, and the narrow leaves turn gold in fall like other Amsonia. Its smaller stature suits a mid-border spot where full-size bluestar would be too large, and it needs no staking despite the wiry, upright habit. Grow in average to moist, well-drained soil in full sun for the best flowering and fall color.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring into well-drained soil in full sun; Blue Bonnet was collected near Melissa, Texas, and is the earliest-blooming Baptisia minor clone in the Plant Delights collection.

directions: Blue Bonnet is a Texas-collected selection of dwarf false indigo chosen for flowering earlier in spring than other clones of the species, sending up spikes of deep blue-violet, lupine-like flowers above a tidy, compact mound of blue-green foliage. Its smaller stature compared to larger Baptisia species suits the middle of a sunny border without the sprawling bulk of Baptisia australis. Like other false indigo it develops a long-lived, deep taproot once established, so choose its permanent position carefully and avoid transplanting mature plants. Grow in well-drained soil in full sun, where it tolerates heat and drought with virtually no maintenance once rooted in.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; this dwarf gold-leaf selection was sourced from Japan's Gotemba Nursery.

directions: Gotemba Gold is an extremely dwarf selection of Liriope minor, forming tiny tufts of bright golden-yellow grass-like foliage only a few inches tall, among the smallest lilyturf selections in cultivation. Short spikes of small lavender flowers appear partly hidden in the foliage in summer, secondary to the striking leaf color that holds its gold tone best with a bit of sun exposure. Its miniature scale suits rock gardens, trough plantings, or the front edge of a shaded border where larger Liriope cultivars would overwhelm the space. Grow in well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun and divide congested clumps occasionally to propagate new plants.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into humus-rich, moist, well-drained woodland soil in shade to partial shade; Snowfall is a rare white-flowered selection of the typically maroon-flowered species.

directions: Snowfall is a rare white-flowered form of Chinese mayapple, a dramatic departure from the typical species' maroon blooms, opening clusters of pure white flowers beneath its large, glossy, umbrella-like leaves in spring. The bold, deeply lobed foliage alone makes this a striking architectural accent for a shaded border even between bloom seasons, easily reaching two feet across on a mature plant. Round red fruit sometimes follows the flowers in a good year, adding fall interest above the darkening leaves. Grow in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained woodland soil in shade to partial shade, and give it room to spread into a substantial colony over time.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring into well-drained soil in full sun; this hybrid traces to a 2010 cross of Baptisia alba, australis, albescens, and tinctoria.

directions: Lavender Towers is one of the tallest false indigo hybrids available, sending up dense, upright spikes of mauve-lavender pea-like flowers well over five feet high above a sturdy clump of blue-green foliage. Bred from a complex multi-species cross, it combines the height and vigor of its larger parents with a flower color distinct from the more common blue, yellow, and white Baptisia hybrids. Like other false indigo it develops a long-lived, deep taproot, so site it where it can stay undisturbed for decades once established. Grow in well-drained soil in full sun; established plants tolerate heat and drought and need no staking despite their height.
